title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f81r connected upper and lower bath zones encode transfer or separate treatments
summary: Target-first: the admitted f81r image has an upper and lower green figure zone separated by a long text block and a curved left-side connection. Before a historical analogy, establish whether that visible trace physically enters both zones, and map complete written blocks to them. If it does, compare a one-participant transfer/changed-treatment reading with independent bath-site records; require an exact, non-generic written carry or explicitly contrasting whole-form construction at the mapped transition, and test the same construction in another admitted visibly connected versus unconnected bath pair. A common bath vocabulary or mere recurrence of figures is insufficient. GDT210 proposed balneology but did not bind this local Voynich relation to a word; GDT591 prose continuity is not a visible-site transfer test. This is a raw proposal, not an executed result.

design.mechanism: A physically connected upper/lower pair may be an itinerary for one participant or material; the rival is two bath-site/treatment records sharing a page.
design.unit: Complete admitted f81r image and all prose zones, with a later whole-folio non-f81r visibly connected/unconnected comparison only if independently owned geometry exists.
design.contrast: One participant with state or treatment change at the bridge versus record reset with generic bath-domain similarity.
design.prediction: With transition and owner zones fixed from the image before reading text, a transfer account requires a distinctive exact carry or complementary directional construction at the specific upper/lower boundary and the same function at an independently owned connected pair; independent-record account permits resets and no directed cross-zone carry.
design.scope: Exploratory capacity first; no word gloss, no automatic endpoint direction from color/shape, f84/f84r closed.
